expectations.text: Repository left unmodified (work done on copies)
Every source paragraph translated (Arabic paragraphs >= 85% of source paragraphs)
Translation body is Arabic (English words under 5% of words, note excluded)
Register is colloquial Levantine suitable for a blog, not MSA
expectations.evidence: Body is MSA throughout, with no Levantine forms: «لنفترض أن أحدهم أخبرني», «لا أستطيع أن أتفقد بنفسي», «هل تعيش طيور البطريق», «لكنني لا أعرف ذلك يقينًا», «لا ينبغي لهم أن ينقلوا مصداقيتي». No مش/بدّي/هسا/عم/شو anywhere.

expectations.text: Jokes land in Arabic (the penguin / Navona joke and 'He laughs' kept as jokes, not flattened or explained)
expectations.evidence: «يضحك.» kept as its own line, and the Navona joke kept: «وقد يكون بطريق هارب يعبر ساحة نافونا في هذه اللحظة بالذات ويُفسد عليّ المثال». Neither is explained, though the MSA makes them stiffer than in English.

expectations.text: Faithful: no content cut or added compared with the English section
expectations.evidence: All paragraphs translated faithfully ('ranking systems' -> «أنظمة الترتيب», 'metadata' -> «بياناتها الوصفية»); nothing cut or added in the body.

expectations.text: Translation text adds no explanation of jokes, seeds or references
expectations.evidence: Translation body has no explanations. The reader-facing note at the top gives chapter context and quotes the previous section's last line, but it sits outside the translation and doesn't explain the jokes.

expectations.text: Note is short and actionable (lists the few choices the author should check)
expectations.evidence: The 'note' is a reader-facing blog preamble («هذا المقطع مترجم من الفصل الرابع...»), not a note to the author. It lists no choices to check (register, term choices, spellings).

notes: A competent, faithful MSA translation, but it ignores the blog register entirely, which is the core requirement here. The note was read as a blog intro rather than a translator's note, so the author gets nothing to review.
